text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty ALERT: URGENT — service-discovery SRV lookup error spike in us-east1a. error_rate >= 5% over last 1m. Paging alicia (oncall)

alicia (oncall): On it. jumping in. seeing a bunch of 5xx from coredns in us-east1a and a pile of SRV timeouts in frontend logs.

benj: Also seeing retry storms from worker processes hitting consul in the same AZ. SRV lookups timing out ~2s then retries.

carla: Are we sure this is coredns and not upstream routing? I ran a quick traceroute to the consul leader and hit 300ms spikes + packet loss.

dmitri: Infra check -> peering / egress flaps in us-east1a. Cloud telemetry shows intermittent blackholing to backbone prefixes (10.0.0.0/16). I've opened a ticket with provider. cc: @netops.

netops: Confirming, we're seeing AZ peering flap affecting control-plane meshes. Packets drop for ~30-60s periodically. Opening high-priority cloud support case now.

alicia (oncall): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Shift SRV traffic for critical services off us-east1a -> us-east1b/1c 2) Reduce SRV TTL to 30s so clients re-query quickly 3) Scale coredns in us-east1a to drain queues. Benj, run the failover script and lower TTLs.

benj: Running `./scripts/dns-failover --from us-east1a --to us-east1b --services critical` now. Step 1: reduce TTLs -> `./scripts/set-ttl --zone service.example.com --ttl 30` in flight.

alicia (oncall): Also scaling CoreDNS in us-east1a: `kubectl -n infra scale deploy coredns --replicas=10` to clear the request backlog.

carla: Adding a temporary iptables redirect on app nodes to route consul client traffic via cross-AZ LB (higher latency but prevents timeouts). Pushing change to a subset first.

dmitri: Observed consul leader CPU at 95% and large KV watch backlog. Forcing an election is riskier than leaving it. Recommend switching read traffic to replicas and increase consul client timeout to 5s temporarily.

alicia (oncall): Agreed, no forced election. Benj, please increase client timeout and add retries with exponential backoff in the short term.

benj: Failover script applied. TTL lowered to 30s. Clients should start seeing new SRV responses within one TTL cycle. Monitoring now.

incident-bot: Alert update: SRV error rate dropping -> 5.4% to 1.2% over last 2 minutes.

carla: :thumbsup: frontend error rate falling, still seeing long-tail failures ~0.4%. Keeping canary traffic routed away from us-east1a.

netops: Cloud provider confirms partial fabric instability; they will apply a routing fix. ETA ~12 minutes for full propagation.

alicia (oncall): Keep the failover cut in place until provider confirms stable for 15m. Postmortem owners: alicia (oncall), benj, netops.

dmitri: Action items for follow-up: add SRV lookup latency to SLOs, add client-wise backoff to prevent retry storms, and add runbook step: reduce TTL + run dns-failover.sh for AZ routing failures.

benj: I'll open tracking ticket RW-12345 for the runbook updates, coredns queue alerting, and a post-incident config change to consul client timeouts.

alicia (oncall): Handoff: I'm stepping out for a meeting. carla, you have pager for the next 40m — keep an eye on error rate and coreDNS queue depth.

carla: Got it, taking pager. Will post any spikes.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged. Mitigations in place. Next automated update in 15m or on status change.
